newsitem.title: UK: London Clubs Q1 in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: London Clubs Q1 in line with expectations.

text.p: Casino operator London Clubs International Plc said on Friday the first quarter of its current financial year had been in line with its expectations.
It also said in a statement its expected work on its Aladdin project in Las Vegas to start on schedule in October this year.
It said first quarter business was "similar to the strong levels of trading which were experienced in the same period last year".
The group said the capital raising exercise and contractual negotiations for the planned redevelopment of the Aladdin Hotel and Casino were "progressing well".
In January, London Clubs said it would invest $50 million in cash in the project, the total redevelopment costs for which are estimated to be $750 million over two years.
Under the deal with Aladdin Gaming Corp, London Clubs is to receive a 25 percent equity stake in the hospitality and gaming operations and the underlying real estate.
The company also said in today's statement that two tenders for new casino licences in South Africa had been submitted.

London Clubs, which operates seven casinos in London, is awaiting news on its hostile 190 million stg bid for rival casino operator Capital Corp Plc. The bid was referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) in April. The MMC had to make its recommendation by July 7 to the President of the Board of Trade Margaret Beckett.
A merged company would have control of almost two-thirds of London's 1.7 billion stg casino market -- an increasingly attractive sector as rules on membership and drinking loosen in Britain.
